title: Imperfect Tense
summary: Use the imperfect for habits, background descriptions, and ongoing past situations.

sections.heading: What the imperfect means
sections.body: The **pretérito imperfeito** describes what used to happen, what was happening, or what things were like in the past. It sets the scene rather than presenting a completed event.

examples.pt: Quando eu era criança, morava em Belo Horizonte.
examples.en: When I was a child, I lived in Belo Horizonte.
It was raining a lot that week.

examples.pt: A gente sempre almoçava na casa da minha avó.
examples.en: We always used to have lunch at my grandmother's house.

sections.heading: Regular forms
sections.body:
Regular **-ar** verbs use **-ava** endings; **-er/-ir** verbs use **-ia** endings. The eu and você/ele/ela forms are identical, but the full paradigm is still useful.

| Subject | falar | comer | abrir |
|---|---|---|---|
| eu | **falava** | **comia** | **abria** |
| você/ele/ela | **falava** | **comia** | **abria** |
| nós | **falávamos** | **comíamos** | **abríamos** |
| vocês/eles/elas | **falavam** | **comiam** | **abriam** |

examples.en: I used to study in the morning.

examples.pt: Eles abriam a loja às nove.
examples.en: They used to open the store at nine.

sections.heading: Irregular imperfect forms
sections.body: Only a few common verbs are irregular in the imperfect: **ser → era**, **ter → tinha**, **vir → vinha**, and **pôr → punha**.

examples.en: He used to come here every Sunday.

keyPoints: Use the imperfect for habits, background, age, time, and ongoing past states.
-ar verbs use -ava endings; -er/-ir verbs use -ia endings.
The eu and você/ele/ela forms are identical in the regular imperfect.
Ser, ter, vir, and pôr are the main irregular imperfect verbs.
Preterite advances the story; imperfect describes the setting.

commonMistakes.note: Childhood/background uses the imperfect of ser.

commonMistakes.wrong: Eu comi na escola todos os dias.
commonMistakes.right: Eu comia na escola todos os dias.
